mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por)
bivar: Bivar — Vivar, the Cid's home village just north of Burgos
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado)
ojo: ojo — eye; a ojo 'in plain sight'
ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished')
tornós: tornar + se — she turned back (tornó + -s(e): after a stressed vowel -se shrinks to -s)
manol: mano + le — hand + to him (enclitic le reduced to l)
fabló: fablar — he spoke (preterite; = habló, note f-)
voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly'
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold')
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least'
algún: alguno — some, any (apocopated before a noun; = algún)
far: far — to do (apocopated infinitive of fazer; = hacer)
plazdo: plazdo — term, time limit, appointed day (= plazo)
an: aver — they have (3rd pl. present of aver = han)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!'
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida)
exido: exir — gone out (past part.; exido es 'has gone out', ser as perfect auxiliary)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus)
aver: aver — wealth, property, goods (noun use of aver, beside aver the verb 'to have')
trayo: traer — I carry, bring (present 1st sg.; = traigo)
dar: dar — to give (infinitive; split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como)
san: santo — Saint (apocopated before a name; = san)
pero: Pero — Peter (San Pero = San Pedro, the saint of the monastery)
matines: matín — matins, the early-morning office of prayer (pl.; = maitines)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us')
santa: santo — Saint (fem.); Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing'
pienssan: pensar — they think; pensar de + inf. 'to set about (doing)' (epic formula)
tañen: tañer — they ring, toll (present 3rd pl.; = tañen)
doña: doña — lady (title; Latin domina, fem. of don)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto)
ella: ella — she, her (stressed 3rd sg. fem. pronoun)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already'
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
maría: María — Mary; Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something')
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied')
fablar: fablar — to speak (infinitive; = hablar, note f-)
vino: vino — wine (noun); also venir — he came (strong preterite 3rd sg.; por en vino a aquesto, 'that is how he came to this pass')
do: do — where, as (relative adverb, Latin de ubi; = donde)
señas: señas — one each, one apiece (distributive adjective, fem. pl., Latin singulas; = sendas)
partes: parte — part, quarter, direction (pl.); de todas partes 'from every quarter'
uno: uno — one; en uno = 'together, as one'
era: seer — it was (imperfect of seer = ser)
lança: lança — lance (= lanza); ardida lança, 'bold lance', stands for the bold man who wields it
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding
llególas: llegar + las — he brought them close (preterite 3rd sg. llegó + enclitic las; = las llegó)
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour'
salvo: salvo — safety, safe-keeping (noun; en vuestro salvo 'in your safe keeping')
santos: santo — saint (masc. pl.); los sos santos 'his saints'
tú: tú — thou, you (2nd sg. subject pronoun; used in prayer to God)
ayude: ayudar — may she help (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
fecha: fazer — made, done (past part. fem. of fazer = hacer; = hecha, note f-)
quieren: querer — they wish, are about to (present 3rd pl.)
acomiendo: acomendar — I entrust, commend (present 1st sg.; = encomiendo)
unos: uno — some (masc. pl.; unos … otros 'some … others')
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena)
myo: mio — my (unstressed possessive, variant spelling of mio)
cabeça: cabeça — head (= cabeza; ç sounded ts)
sabor: sabor — pleasure, wish; a so sabor 'at his (their) pleasure'
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
sea: seer — may be, that is (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
aun: aun — even, besides · also aun — yet, still (aun vea el dia 'may I yet see the day')
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift')
sancho: Sancho — the abbot of San Pedro de Cardeña
castigar: castigar — to instruct, advise (infinitive; castigar los he = 'I shall instruct them', split future)
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?')
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán)
çerca: çerca — near; here adverbial, çerca o tarde = 'sooner or later' (= cerca)
passó: passar — he passed, crossed (preterite 3rd sg.; = pasó)
sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas)
